newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Axa buys Generali's 11 pct stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Axa buys Generali's 11 pct stake.

text.p: Insurer Axa bought out on Friday Italian insurer Generali's 11 percent stake in the French company for 5.9 billion francs, bringing down the curtain on their co-operation efforts.
Generali, Italy's largest insurer, sold its Axa stake as it no longer saw it as a strategic holding and Axa exercised its preemptive right to buy the stock, the two companies said.
Generali had long been unhappy over its Axa stake, last year threatening to sell if it did not become a more active partner.

In February, Axa announced a restructuring under which Generali transformed its indirect holding in Axa into a direct holding, making it more liquid. And in March, the two signed a shareholder cooperation pact to run unto the year 2000.
"It's true we didn't expect them to sell so quickly," an Axa official said.
The two groups had intended to cooperate internationally with Generali expressing keen interest in developing mutual ventures in Asia where Axa has built a strong foothold.
But these never materialised. "There were no opportunities," said an Axa spokeswoman. Generali said it had nothing to add to the companies' joint statement.

Axa said the purchase eliminated the risk of big amounts of its stock coming onto the market and weighing on the price and said the transaction would boost earnings per share (EPS) as it planned to cancel the shares it had bought.
One analyst calculated EPS would rise by 2.5 percent as a result. "The effect is like a U.S.-style buyback," said one.
Axa shares rose 4.1 francs to 289.10 on the announcement.
"There was concern it (the stake) might have gone on the market but they've bypassed the market," said one broker.
Shares in Generali were up 205 lira at 33,100.

The purchase was carried out at a minimum price of 285 francs per share which the two said gave Generali "a significant capital gain" as it began buying Axa shares from 1988 at an average price of 250 francs.
Axa was reported to have offered to buy the Italian group's stake in July for 285 francs but at that time, Generali refused, arguing it was capable of showing a strong rise in value.

Axa chairman Claude Bebear said then Axa's talks with Generali had not produced "any significant collaboration" of the kind sought by the Italian group. Axa said, however, on Friday "considering the good relationship between both groups," it had asked company chairman Antoine Bernheim to stay on its board.
